answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks with a staked bond tied to a persistent identity. An agent locks real value before attesting, and votes are weighted by stake, so splitting one wallet into fifty puppets fractures the funds into shares too small to sway outcomes. When a cluster of fresh keys votes in lockstep, the protocol slashes the group, so the attacker forfeits capital. Influence costs funds that detection confiscates, so attackers risk more than they gain, while a fabricated ivory identity never inherits trust built over a long voyage, leaving a fake reef worth less than its stake.
